idiom_name: readonly value type with same-type methods (add(a: Money, b: Money): Money) and branded units
implementation_notes: The runtime is JavaScript, so + cannot be overloaded and the closed operation must be a function or method; TypeScript's contribution is the type contract that keeps it closed: declare the value as a readonly type (readonly fields, Readonly<T> or a frozen object literal) and give the operation the signature (a: Money, b: Money) => Money, so call sites cannot silently fall back to numbers. What replaces the classic structure is that readonly type plus same-type operations and a factory that validates and brands the value - structural typing means an unrelated object of the same shape is assignable, so a unique symbol brand or a private field is what actually prevents mixing currencies or units. Named methods remain for non-arithmetic combinations (union, intersect), exactly as in JavaScript.
pitfalls: readonly, Readonly<T> and brands are erased at runtime: data parsed from JSON or structuredClone arrives unvalidated and untyped, so re-validate at the boundary before treating it as a value.
Structural typing accepts any object with the same shape; without a brand, a Duration or a plain { minor, currency } literal passes as Money and the 'closure' silently combines different domains.
bigint and number do not mix (1n + 1 throws) - choose one representation for minor units everywhere, including in JSON payloads where bigint does not survive JSON.stringify by default.
Returning object literals loses class identity, so instanceof checks and prototype methods are unavailable later; if you need them, use classes with readonly fields and keep the same-type signature.
